claim: examples[0] shows `.loop   altgb   ptr, ##$100              ' Auto-increment by 1` followed by `getbyte char, 0-0, #0`, and the notes say 'Auto-increment feature useful for sequential access'. ALTGB D,{#}S sets the next S field to (D[10:2] + S) & $1FF and N to D[1:0], and ADDS sign-extended S[17:9] to D. `##$100` has S[8:0] = $100 (adds 256 to the register index) and S[17:9] = 0, so D is NOT incremented; the loop would re-read the same byte. Incrementing D by 1 needs S[17:9] = 1, e.g. `##$200`. The block compiles either way, so the gate cannot see it (scratch cases1.py altgb_inc: `altgb ptr, ##$200` compiles).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:132 (`ALTGB D,{#}S` ... `D += sign-extended S[17:9]`)

claim: examples[3] gives `COGINIT #HUBEXEC+5, PTRA` then `SETQ ptra_val  'ptra_val will go into target cog's PTRA register`; examples[4] gives `COGINIT #%0_1_0000, addr` then `--or--` / `SETQ ptra_val`. SETQ must come BEFORE the COGINIT to supply the new cog's PTRA (the silicon doc says 'If COGINIT is preceded by SETQ, the SETQ value will be written into the target cog's PTRA register'; its listing has `SETQ ptra_val` on the line before `COGINIT #%0_1_0000,addr`). As written, the SETQ follows the COGINIT and has no effect on it (the new cog gets PTRA = 0).

`mov flag, FALSE`, `if_e mov flag, TRUE` (false.yaml), `mov result, TRUE`, `if_z mov result, FALSE` (true.yaml) and `cmps value, NEGX wc`, `mov limit, NEGX` (negx.yaml) give a value constant as the S operand with no `#`/`##`, so S is a REGISTER ADDRESS. All compile, none does what the comments say. Assembled (pnut-ts, scratch cases4.py a_true, od of main.bin): `mov flag, TRUE` -> $FFFF_FFFF (the -1 is OR-ed over the whole instruction word; not a MOV at all), `mov flag, FALSE` -> $F600_0C00, byte-identical to `mov flag, 0` (copies cog register 0), `cmps flag, NEGX wc` -> $F250_0C00, identical to `cmps flag, 0 wc`. The same error in posx.yaml:18, :24 is caught by the compiler (registered class S-PENDING-const-as-register-operand). Correct forms: `mov flag, #0`, `neg flag, #1` or `mov flag, ##TRUE`, `cmps value, ##NEGX wc`.
source: scratch cases4.py a_true (od -A d -t x4 main.bin: ffffffff f6000dff f6000c00 f6000c00 f2500c00 f2500c00); silicon-doc-text.txt (`#` immediate is 9 bits, `##` augments)

claim: examples[2] runs `cmp a, b wcz  ' Set both C and Z` and then `if_c_and_z    DEBUG("a == b AND overflow")`. After CMP, C = (a < b) and Z = (a == b); they cannot both be 1, so the branch never fires, and 'overflow' is not what C means for CMP. The condition list at :19 ('IF_C_AND_Z - Both carry and zero set') is fine in itself; the example label is the defect.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv (CMP: C = borrow, Z = equal)

claim: 'Available in v47+' / 'Prior to v47, conditions before DEBUG caused compile errors'. The v55 change log has no such line in its v47 row (spin2-v55-text.txt:39); the sentence 'PASM DEBUG instructions can be now preceded by a condition, not just a _RET_' sits at :61-64, after the v50 row (:42) and before the v51 heading (:66), i.e. v50-era, not v47.

examples[1] 'Detect rising edge (0->1 transition)': `testp input_pin wc ' Get current state` then `if_nc_and_z jmp #edge_detected ' Was 0, now 1`. After TESTP ... WC, C is the pin's CURRENT state, so `if_nc` means the pin is LOW now; Z is a stale flag from earlier code. The branch fires on 'low and Z set', not on a rising edge, and `muxz flag_reg,#1` then stores Z, not the pin state. examples[2] (:76-80) comments `testp sensor_pin wz   ' Test pin, XOR with C`: WZ only writes Z = pin state; the XOR form is XORZ (TESTP {#}D WC/WZ/ANDC/ANDZ/ORC/ORZ/XORC/XORZ). Both compile.

examples[2] 'Extract exponent and mantissa parts': `GETQX log_result`, `SHR log_result, #27 WZ` (turns log_result into the exponent, destroying the mantissa bits), `MOV exponent, log_result`, then `AND mantissa, ##$07FFFFFF ' Extract 27-bit mantissa`. `mantissa` is never loaded: the AND masks an uninitialised register. The mantissa has to be taken from the unshifted value (`mov mantissa, log_result` / `and mantissa, ##$07FFFFFF` BEFORE the SHR). Compiles.

`algorithm.operation` gives XORO32 as three steps on a 32-bit D (`D ^= D >> 2`, `D ^= D << 1`, `D ^= D >> 1`) under the name 'xoroshiro32+'. Neither the instruction table nor the silicon doc gives these steps (they say only 'Iterate D with xoroshiro32+ PRNG algorithm and put PRNG result into next instruction's S'); a three-step xorshift is not the xoroshiro32+ update. Also unsourced: 'Never produces zero from non-zero seed', 'Good statistical properties'. :74-76 repeat the GETRND 'true randomness from thermal noise / cryptographically suitable' claim (class S-023). The 'zero seed returns zero forever' warning at :30-34 is consistent with a xorshift-style generator but also unsourced.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv/P2 Instructions v35 - Rev B_C Silicon - Sheet1.csv:413; silicon-doc-text.txt:1183

claim: examples[3] 'Acquire multiple locks in order' returns its outcome by `setd .result, #1` / `setd .result, #0` where `.result ret` is the routine's own RET instruction. SETD rewrites the D field of that instruction word; RET has no D operand and nothing reads that field back, so the caller receives no result, and the routine modifies its own code (not re-entrant, and the next call starts with whatever D the last call left). Compiles.
source: the block itself; engineering/ingestion/sources/p2-instructions-csv (RET has no D operand)

claim: examples[0] comments `FIT $1F0 ' Ensure code fits before the special-register area` and the notes call $1F0 'user area before special registers'. $1F0..$1F7 are dual-purpose registers (general RAM unless INT1-3/CALLD-imm functions are used); the special-purpose registers are $1F8..$1FF. examples[1] on the same page (`FIT $1F8`) is the correct limit for 'before the special registers'.

`oneliner: Set hub execution mode for subsequent code`. HUBEXEC is a predefined constant (`value: '%10_0000'`) added into COGINIT's D operand; it sets nothing 'for subsequent code' (compare cogexec.yaml:36 'Predefined constant for COGINIT instruction').
source: language/pasm2/hubexec.yaml:1-16 (the page's own description and value); silicon-doc-text.txt:376-379

claim: `encoding: TBD`, `timing: cycles: TBD, type: TBD`, `documentation_level: minimal`, description 'Debug instruction. Provides debugging functionality during program execution.' -- the page serves placeholders where an encoding and timing belong, and its only example is the bare word `DEBUG` (a statement that does nothing without arguments unless compiled with -d; scratch cases3.py: 0 bytes without -d, 2938 bytes with -d).

'High-Speed Data Reception' shows `xinit wmode, #0` with `wmode = $C081_0000 + spi_do<<17`. The count field D[15:0] of that value is 0, and a streamer count of 0 means the streamer does not run. In the source this example is taken from, the count is patched in first (`setword wmode,x,#0 'insert into streamer command`, flash_loader.spin2:255); the page omits that line. The page's other two examples carry their counts in the constant ($0800, $0008).

pnut-ts accepts `mov flag, TRUE` (S = -1) and emits $FFFF_FFFF, while `cmp value, POSX` is rejected with 'Register cannot exceed $1FF'. The register-operand range check apparently treats negative values as in range (and `NEGX` = $8000_0000 is silently reduced to 0). Reported as a DEVIATION item as well; no KB change follows from it beyond O3.
